review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

9:1.sourceText: Περὶ μὲν γὰρ τῆς διακονίας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους περισσόν μοί ἐστιν τὸ γράφειν ὑμῖν·
9:1.targetText: Now about the service to the saints, there is no need for me to write to you.

groups.note: The connective γάρ ("for") is rendered Now.
περισσόν ("superfluous") is rendered no need.
The article τό with the infinitive γράφειν is rendered to write.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:2.sourceText: οἶδα γὰρ τὴν προθυμίαν ὑμῶν ἣν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καυχῶμαι Μακεδόσιν ὅτι Ἀχαΐα παρεσκεύασται ἀπὸ πέρυσι, καὶ τὸ ὑμῶν ζῆλος ἠρέθισεν τοὺς πλείονας.
9:2.targetText: For I know your eagerness to help, and I have been boasting to the Macedonians that since last year you in Achaia were prepared to give. And your zeal has stirred most of them to do likewise.

groups.note: The relative ἥν ("which") is rendered and, as BSB starts a new clause.
BSB merges ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ("about you") into the subject you in Achaia.
τοὺς πλείονας ("the majority") is rendered most.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB merges ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν into the subject you, so ὑπέρ has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds what the eagerness is for; the Greek has only the noun.
English adds what Achaia was prepared to do; the Greek verb has no such complement.
English adds a partitive phrase; the Greek has no pronoun here.
English completes the sense of stirred; the Greek has no further verb.

9:3.sourceText: ἔπεμψα δὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς, ἵνα μὴ τὸ καύχημα ἡμῶν τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν κενωθῇ ἐν τῷ μέρει τούτῳ, ἵνα καθὼς ἔλεγον παρεσκευασμένοι ἦτε,
9:3.targetText: But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said.

groups.note: The aorist ἔπεμψα ("I sent") is rendered I am sending.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds but to contrast the two purpose clauses; the Greek has no connective here.

9:4.sourceText: μή πως ἐὰν ἔλθωσιν σὺν ἐμοὶ Μακεδόνες καὶ εὕρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἀπαρασκευάστους καταισχυνθῶμεν ἡμεῖς, ἵνα μὴ λέγωμεν ὑμεῖς, ἐν τῇ ὑποστάσει ταύτῃ.
9:4.targetText: Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—to say nothing of you—would be ashamed of having been so confident.

groups.note: μή πως ("lest somehow") is rendered Otherwise.
ὑποστάσει ("confidence") is rendered as the adjective confident.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English turns the noun ὑποστάσει into a verbal phrase; the Greek has no verb here.

9:5.sourceText: ἀναγκαῖον οὖν ἡγησάμην παρακαλέσαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἵνα προέλθωσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς καὶ προκαταρτίσωσιν τὴν προεπηγγελμένην εὐλογίαν ὑμῶν, ταύτην ἑτοίμην εἶναι οὕτως ὡς εὐλογίαν καὶ μὴ ὡς πλεονεξίαν.
9:5.targetText: So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to visit you beforehand and make arrangements for the bountiful gift you had promised. This way, your gift will be prepared generously and not begrudgingly.

groups.note: προέλθωσιν ("go ahead") is rendered visit … beforehand.
εὐλογίαν ("blessing") is rendered bountiful gift.
BSB renders your promised gift as the gift you had promised.
ταύτην ("this") is rendered by its referent, your gift.
ὡς εὐλογίαν ("as a blessing") is rendered generously.
ὡς πλεονεξίαν ("as greed") is rendered begrudgingly.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes εἰς ὑμᾶς ("to you") the object of visit, so εἰς has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the anticipatory it; the Greek has no pronoun here.

9:6.sourceText: Τοῦτο δέ, ὁ σπείρων φειδομένως φειδομένως καὶ θερίσει, καὶ ὁ σπείρων ἐπ’ εὐλογίαις ἐπ’ εὐλογίαις καὶ θερίσει.
9:6.targetText: Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.

groups.note: The article with the participle σπείρων ("sowing") is rendered Whoever sows.
The article with the participle σπείρων ("sowing") is rendered whoever sows.
ἐπ’ εὐλογίαις ("with blessings") is rendered generously.
ἐπ’ εὐλογίαις ("with blessings") is rendered generously.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb for the elliptical Τοῦτο δέ ("now this").

9:7.sourceText: ἕκαστος καθὼς προῄρηται τῇ καρδίᾳ, μὴ ἐκ λύπης ἢ ἐξ ἀνάγκης· ἱλαρὸν γὰρ δότην ἀγαπᾷ ὁ Θεός.
9:7.targetText: Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.

groups.note: καθώς ("just as") is rendered what.
The article τῇ is used as a possessive and rendered his.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat out of before compulsion.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; the Greek clause has none.
English repeats the supplied verb; the Greek has no verb here.

9:8.sourceText: δυνατεῖ δὲ ὁ Θεὸς πᾶσαν χάριν περισσεῦσαι εἰς ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἐν παντὶ πάντοτε πᾶσαν αὐτάρκειαν ἔχοντες περισσεύητε εἰς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθόν,
9:8.targetText: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work.

groups.note: The transitive infinitive περισσεῦσαι is rendered make … abound.
πᾶσαν αὐτάρκειαν ("all sufficiency") is rendered all that you need.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English turns the noun αὐτάρκειαν into a clause; the Greek has no relative or pronoun here.

9:9.sourceText: καθὼς γέγραπται Ἐσκόρπισεν, ἔδωκεν τοῖς πένησιν, ἡ δικαιοσύνη αὐτοῦ μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
9:9.targetText: As it is written:  “He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.”

groups.note: ἔδωκεν ("he gave") is rendered His gifts.
εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ("into the age") is rendered forever.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:10.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἐπιχορηγῶν σπέρμα τῷ σπείροντι καὶ ἄρτον εἰς βρῶσιν χορηγήσει καὶ πληθυνεῖ τὸν σπόρον ὑμῶν καὶ αὐξήσει τὰ γενήματα τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὑμῶν·
9:10.targetText: Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your store of seed and will increase the harvest of your righteousness.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἐπιχορηγῶν ("supplying") is rendered He who supplies.
Same meaning; BSB's Greek has a different word for seed here.
The article with the participle σπείροντι ("sowing") is rendered to the sower.
σπόρον ("seed for sowing") is rendered store of seed.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:11.sourceText: ἐν παντὶ πλουτιζόμενοι εἰς πᾶσαν ἁπλότητα, ἥτις κατεργάζεται δι’ ἡμῶν εὐχαριστίαν τῷ Θεῷ.
9:11.targetText: You will be enriched in every way to be generous on every occasion, so that through us your giving will produce thanksgiving to God.

groups.note: πᾶσαν ("all") is rendered on every occasion.
ἁπλότητα ("generosity") is rendered as the adjective generous.
The relative ἥτις ("which"), referring to the generosity, is rendered your giving.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes the participle a finite clause; the Greek participle has no person or future.
English supplies a copula with generous; the Greek has the noun ἁπλότητα.
English adds a result connective; the Greek continues with the relative ἥτις.

9:12.sourceText: ὅτι ἡ διακονία τῆς λειτουργίας ταύτης οὐ μόνον ἐστὶν προσαναπληροῦσα τὰ ὑστερήματα τῶν ἁγίων, ἀλλὰ καὶ περισσεύουσα διὰ πολλῶν εὐχαριστιῶν τῷ Θεῷ·
9:12.targetText: For this ministry of service is not only supplying the needs of the saints, but is also overflowing in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.

groups.note: ταύτης goes with service in the Greek; BSB places this before ministry.
The one ἐστίν serves both participles; BSB repeats is.
The plural εὐχαριστιῶν ("thanksgivings") is rendered expressions of thanksgiving.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:13.sourceText: διὰ τῆς δοκιμῆς τῆς διακονίας ταύτης δοξάζοντες τὸν Θεὸν ἐπὶ τῇ ὑποταγῇ τῆς ὁμολογίας ὑμῶν εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἁπλότητι τῆς κοινωνίας εἰς αὐτοὺς καὶ εἰς πάντας,
9:13.targetText: Because of the proof this ministry provides, the saints will glorify God for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ, and for the generosity of your contribution to them and to all the others.

groups.note: ὑποταγῇ ("obedience") is rendered as the adjective obedient.
The article τῆς is used as a possessive and rendered your.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English recasts the genitive τῆς διακονίας ταύτης ("of this ministry") as a clause; the Greek has no verb here.
English names the subject of the participle δοξάζοντες; the Greek has no noun here.
English adds a future; the participle δοξάζοντες has no person or tense of its own.
English adds others to complete all; the Greek has only πάντας.

9:14.sourceText: καὶ αὐτῶν δεήσει ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐπιποθούντων ὑμᾶς διὰ τὴν ὑπερβάλλουσαν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐφ’ ὑμῖν.
9:14.targetText: And their prayers for you will express their affection for you, because of the surpassing grace God has given you.

groups.note: αὐτῶν is the subject of ἐπιποθούντων; BSB renders it with both prayers and affection.
The participle ἐπιποθούντων ("longing for") is rendered as the noun affection.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB recasts ἐφ’ ὑμῖν ("upon you") as God has given you, so ἐφ’ has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb that makes their prayers the subject; the Greek has only the participle ἐπιποθούντων ("longing for"), with no verb meaning express and no future.
English supplies a verb for ἐφ’ ὑμῖν ("upon you"); the Greek has no verb here.

9:15.sourceText: Χάρις τῷ Θεῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἀνεκδιηγήτῳ αὐτοῦ δωρεᾷ.
9:15.targetText: Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb of the exclamation.
